titulo: Mapping frameworks for synthesizing qualitative evidence in health technology assessment
titulo_curto: Listening to patients in health decisions: how to bring qualitative research together

revista.nome: International Journal of Technology Assessment in Health Care

em_1_minuto.titulo: Decisions that look only at numbers
em_1_minuto.texto: To decide whether a treatment enters a health system, people usually look at efficacy and cost. Qualitative research shows another side: what patients, families and professionals experience and think.
In a scoping review, they searched 10 databases and agency websites for every document that teaches how to bring qualitative research into these decisions.
Of 2,054 records, 31 documents were included. Most came from Europe, and almost half were guides. Few explain the whole process, from start to finish.

em_1_minuto.titulo: Giving a voice to those who use the system
em_1_minuto.texto: Standardizing the use of qualitative evidence can make decisions more complete, taking into account acceptability, feasibility and equity.

secoes.titulo: Why listen to people in decisions about technologies
secoes.lede: An assessment is stronger when it combines numbers and experiences.

blocos.html:
Health technology assessment (HTA) studies the value of drugs, tests, equipment and programs to guide decisions in a fair and efficient health system. Traditionally, it gives more weight to efficacy and costs.

Qualitative evidence, which comes from interviews, focus groups and observation, explains why an intervention works or not, from people's point of view. Combining several studies of this kind, in a qualitative evidence synthesis, produces stronger evidence than any single study.

itens.texto: Do people accept this treatment? How do they feel when using it?
Can it be applied in practice, in real services?
Do all groups have fair access?
What matters to patients, families and professionals?

blocos.html: A recent study showed that, although the patient perspective appears often in submissions to the agencies of the UK (NICE) and Canada (CADTH), only 14 of 107 and 24 of 124 of them, respectively, collected qualitative data formally.

secoes.lede: A scoping review maps everything that exists on a topic, without judging a single result.

itens.texto: The plan was registered on the OSF platform and published in advance, following the PRISMA rules for scoping reviews.
Up to June 2023, in Medline, LILACS, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, Cochrane, JBI and ScienceDirect, plus grey literature and HTA agency websites. No year limit, in six languages.
Two independent reviewers read titles, abstracts and full texts; a third resolved disagreements.
Of the 2,054 records, 57 were read in full and 17 were eligible. Another 9 came from agencies and thesis databases and 5 from reference lists: 31 documents in total.

itens.titulo: Talking with people who live the topic
itens.texto: Patients, members of HTA units and experts in qualitative research were invited to discuss the results.

secoes.lede: See what types of documents exist and how interest in the topic has grown.

parametros.leitura: Almost half of the documents are guides. “Other” includes 2 book chapters, 1 handbook and 2 papers.
No document is from 2010 or earlier. 2018 alone had 7 publications (23%), and interest kept growing afterward.

itens.texto: The most recommended acronym for building the question: setting, perspective, intervention, comparison and evaluation.
The most cited tool for deciding how to do the synthesis, based on the question, time, resources and audience.
The most used method: grouping the studies' findings into common themes.
The most cited tool for checking the quality of each qualitative study.
The main tool for stating how much each finding of the synthesis can be trusted.
The most cited guide for writing up the synthesis transparently.
The only framework cited for turning evidence into recommendations, considering efficacy, resources, acceptability, feasibility and equity.

blocos.html: The steps above bring together the most cited tools at each stage. No single document, however, covers all of them.

secoes.titulo: Many recognize the importance, few explain how to do it
secoes.lede: The path exists in pieces, scattered across several documents.

blocos.html:
Experienced agencies such as NICE (England), SMC (Scotland) and SBU (Sweden) state in their guides that it is important to consider qualitative data. But only three agency documents, from Sweden, Scotland and Germany, explain how to carry out the process.

Most documents describe only one step: the question, the quality appraisal, the synthesis or the recommendation. According to the authors, including qualitative data strengthens the interdisciplinary nature of HTA and broadens the information that supports decisions.
Standardizing the way qualitative evidence is incorporated into HTA can improve decisions and ensure that the experience of patients and families is taken into account systematically.

secoes.titulo: What the study allows us to say
secoes.lede: A growing movement that still needs a single path.

blocos.html: The mapping shows a movement to incorporate qualitative evidence into HTA using specific frameworks. Despite the similarities, most documents describe only part of the process. The findings offer essential considerations for those who carry out technology assessment, including in Brazil.

glossario.def: Health technology assessment: the study of the value of a treatment, test or program to guide decisions.
Knowledge from interviews, focus groups and observation about people's experiences, opinions and values.
A review that gathers and combines the findings of several qualitative studies.
A review that maps what exists on a topic and identifies gaps.
Documents outside scientific journals, such as agency reports, theses and handbooks.
Acronym for building qualitative questions: setting, perspective, intervention, comparison and evaluation.
Criteria for choosing the synthesis method: review question, epistemology, time, resources, expertise, audience and type of data.
A method that organizes the findings of several studies into common themes.
A checklist of questions for appraising the quality of a study.
A tool for rating how much a finding from a qualitative synthesis can be trusted.
A guide for transparently reporting a synthesis of qualitative research.
The “evidence to decision” framework, which helps turn evidence into recommendations.
National Institute for Health and Care Excellence, England's HTA agency.
